newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears control of UK's Birmingham airport.
newsitem.headline: EU clears control of UK's Birmingham airport.

text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had cleared a proposal for a joint venture through which Birmingham International Airport will be controlled by Natwest Ventures Ltd, AER Rianta International and seven district councils of the British west midlands.

The Commission said in a statement that the deal would not result in creation or strengthening of a dominant position. It particularly noted that Irish airport operator AER Rianta has currently no other airport operation activities in the UK as its European activities are confined to Dublin, Shannon and Cork airports in Ireland.
Birmingham airport is Britain's fifth largest in terms of total passenger traffic and third largest in terms of charter passengers.

The district councils are already shareholders in the two companies which currently operate and manage the airport. AER Rianta and financial investment firm Natwest will bring to the project funding and and skills to expand the airport's terminal capacity to accomodate the expected doubling of the number of passengers by the year 2010, the Commission said. -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
